newsitem.title: HUNGARY: BRAU TO MERGE HUNGARY UNITS, OFFERS BUYOUT.
newsitem.headline: BRAU TO MERGE HUNGARY UNITS, OFFERS BUYOUT.

text.p: Austrian brewery Brau Union AG will propose the merger of its two Hungarian units, Martfu and Soproni Sorgyar to make its Hungarian operations more successful, Brau officials said.
"In future we want to be even more successful and to improve by utilising existing synergies," Walther Sachs, Brau Union's board member told a news conference in Budapest.
"For this reason Brau Union will recommend the annual shareholder meetings on April 24th and 25th to merge the two companies."
The Budapest Stock Exchange suspended trading in Martfu and Sopron shares for the day as news of the planned merger were not available yet to a wide range of investors.
Brau Union announced Thursday morning a buyout offer to all Martfu shareholders at 206 Austrian schillings per share.
This price exceeds the previous six months' weighted average price of 2,092 forints on the bourse by more than 43 percent. The offer period runs from February 5 to April 29.
"In the process of merging the two companies...we will offer to all Martfu shareholders to purchase their shares at a price of 206 Austrian schillings," Sachs said.
"When we merge Martfu and Sopron, Martfu ordinary shares will be converted into Sopron ordinary shares and the Sopron ordinary shares will not be listed as they are not listed now."
On the Budapest bourse Sopron lists only its preference shares and these preference shares will remain listed.
Both Martfu and Sopron have been operating successfully in the past and their combined market share has grown to 21 percent by the end of 1996 from 13 percent in 1991, a statement said.
Preliminary 1996 results have not yet been available for either companies as Budapest-listed firms have to release their figures by February 15.
In the first nine months of 1996 Sopron generated a pre-tax profit of 696 million forints, while Martfu had a pre-tax profit of 342 million in the first half of 1996.
Martfu, with its shares in the listed "B" category of the bourse, has to release results only twice a year, unlike listed "A" companies which are required figures quarterly.
